deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page sets up the mechanical theory of heat, with Q the heat supplied to a body and dQ = M dv + N dt in terms of volume v and temperature t. This page derives, in the style of Clausius (1850–1854), the two main theorems and the existence of entropy, and then sketches a Carnot cycle.

(1) First law: A Q = A U + W. Here A is the mechanical equivalent (work per unit heat), U is the internal heat or energy (the script letter) and W is the external work, with dW = p dv. With dQ = M dv + N dt this gives A M = A ∂U/∂v + p and A N = A ∂U/∂t.
[My step] Eliminating U by equality of mixed partials gives
(2) A(∂M/∂t − ∂N/∂v) = ∂p/∂t.
This is Clausius's first fundamental equation.

Side remark M = p/A: this is the ideal-gas case (Mariotte–Gay-Lussac law plus U independent of v, i.e. ∂U/∂v = 0, so A M = p).

Second theorem (Carnot, as recast by Clausius): μ M = ∂p/∂t, where μ is Carnot's function, independent of the substance. It is stated here, not derived. Evaluating μ on an ideal gas, p = R(a+t)/v with a ≈ 273 the absolute zero offset, and M = p/A:
μ = A (∂p/∂t)/p = A/(a+t).

Combining the two theorems: ∂M/∂t − ∂N/∂v − (μ/A) M = 0.

Integrating factor: look for λ = λ(t) such that λ dQ is exact. One has
λ ∂M/∂t − λ ∂N/∂v + (∂λ/∂t) M = 0
provided −λ μ/A = ∂λ/∂t, i.e. λ'/λ = −1/(a+t).
[My step] So λ = C/(a+t), proportional to 1/T with absolute temperature T = a+t.
Then ∂(λM)/∂t − ∂(λN)/∂v = 0. This is exactly the integrability condition for λM dv + λN dt, so
∫ λ (M dv + N dt) = f(v,t)
is a state function: dQ/T is exact, i.e. entropy.

Lower part, a sketch of a Carnot cycle:
- start in state (t, v);
- at t1, in contact with body K1, the substance takes up (aufnehmen) heat Q1;
- an adiabatic change brings it to t2;
- at t2, in contact with K2, it is compressed (zusammendrücken) and gives off heat (written −Q1);
- it reaches (t2, v4);
- it returns adiabatically to (t1, v).
The note K1 ⌣ K2 indicates the net transfer of heat from K1 to K2. This is the standard setting for proving that μ is universal.
errors: μ M = ∂p/∂t is used without derivation on this page (it is Carnot's theorem in Clausius's form); the page records it rather than proving it.
M = p/A holds only for an ideal gas with internal energy independent of volume. It is legitimately used only to evaluate the universal function μ, but is not marked as such.
In the cycle sketch the heat at K2 is written −Q1. In general the heat rejected differs from Q1 (Q1 − Q2 = A W); this is likely a shorthand or slip.
The step from ∂λ/∂t = −λμ/A to λ = C/(a+t) and ∂λ/∂v = 0 is implicit. It is correct because μ depends on t only.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard lecture-style exposition of Clausius's thermodynamics (first law, Carnot function, 1/T as integrating factor, Carnot cycle). It shows Riemann studied or taught the mechanical theory of heat, but contains nothing beyond Clausius.
